name: Rehum
overview: Rehum was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as a descendant of Aaron. He is noted among the priests who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, playing a role in the post-exilic restoration of the priesthood. His designation as a priest underscores his Levitical heritage and service in the temple.
namesAndTitles: The name Rehum means '[he] is compassionate,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name without indication that it was given directly by God. This meaning offers a glimpse into the character or hoped-for qualities associated with him in biblical tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Rehum was a descendant of Aaron, linking him to the priestly lineage central to Israel's worship. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Rehum's significance lies in his role as one of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel, marking him as part of the faithful remnant restoring temple worship after the Babylonian exile. As a descendant of Aaron, his participation highlights the continuity of the Levitical priesthood during a critical period of spiritual renewal for Israel.
